Teacher forcing feeds preceding ground-truth target tokens, not output from a larger teacher model. It prevents feeding a wrong prediction into the next training step, reducing within-prefix compounding. Thus A, C and D all misclassify at least one statement.

In the diagram, F and H are the two encoder residual-plus-normalization blocks; M, P and R follow the decoder masked-attention, cross-attention and feed-forward blocks respectively. Sorting gives FHMPR.

L is the first decoder sublayer receiving shifted target representations as Q, K and V; its residual path joins M. A is positional encoding at D, B is the later feed-forward block Q, D is cross-attention O, and E is the output projection S.

The diagram has two positional encodings B and D, two feed-forward blocks G and Q, and five Add & Norm blocks F,H,M,P,R. C appears once at L; D once at O. E is not depicted as a tokenizer (A and C are embedding blocks).

Post-softmax multiplication zeros future weights but leaves allowed weights divided by the sum over all logits, including future logits. Changing future keys therefore changes earlier outputs, violating autoregressive independence (A); B overlooks this indirect dependence. Allowed weights are at most, not at least, their pre-softmax-masked counterparts, so C is false. In the final row all positions are allowed, so both methods coincide (D).
